environment.description: Same application deployed in a hardened Kubernetes pod. The pod spec applies a custom seccomp profile (located at /var/lib/kubelet/seccomp/profiles/backup-svc.json) that permits only: read, write, openat, close, fstat, mmap, mprotect, munmap, brk, rt_sigaction, rt_sigprocmask, ioctl, access, pipe, select, sched_yield, clone, execve, wait4, kill, fcntl, getdents64, getcwd, chdir, stat, lstat, getpid, getuid, getgid, geteuid, getegid, arch_prctl, futex, set_tid_address, set_robust_list, epoll_create1, epoll_ctl, epoll_wait, socket, connect, bind, listen, accept4, sendto, recvfrom, setsockopt, getsockopt, getpeername, getsockname, nanosleep, clock_gettime, exit_group, sigaltstack, getrandom. Crucially, the profile sets defaultAction to SCMP_ACT_ERRNO with errno EPERM. Additionally, the container runs with readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, and the only writable volume is an emptyDir mounted at /tmp with a 10Mi sizeLimit. The /var/backups/db path has NO volume mount, meaning writes to it hit the read-only overlay and fail with EROFS.
